title: Dandiya Raas
summary: A Gujarati stick dance in which pairs and rings of dancers strike painted sticks together in time to a drum, moving in concentric circles.
howToPlay: The sticks are seen from above, four dancers round one painted floor. Four places are lit: the front and back sticks, the left and right sticks, the two corner pairs, and all four together.
Strike the place a closing ring marks, on the beat, so those sticks meet at the centre.
Keep a steady count: the pattern repeats as the circle turns.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Dandiya raas is danced in concentric rings. Each dancer holds a pair of decorated sticks and strikes the sticks of partners in time to a drum beat and a song.
credits: Tradition: dandiya raas of Gujarat; patterns written for this game
